tables.concept: Customer account (trial signup / organisation). This is the outcome entity, one row per account.
Product usage event log at user level: what each user did, when, and for how long.
Lifecycle or onboarding email sends to accounts, with open and click flags. Templates 1 and 2 reach every account; later templates reach progressively fewer.
Geography reference (country or locale) with region and time-zone offset.
Invoice or billing line items for paid subscriptions, recurring roughly monthly.
Subscription plan catalogue: list price, seat capacity and tier.
Paid subscription header, at most one per account. It records which accounts converted to paid, the plan, the start and end times, and the status.
Customer support tickets: open and close times, severity, and CSAT rating.
Users (seats) belonging to accounts, with role, the inviting user and creation time. Exactly one user per account has role_cd=1, probably the account owner or creator.

columns.meaning: Account identifier.
Customer segment code (4 levels, e.g. SMB/mid-market/enterprise). This is not a plan reference.
Account creation time, i.e. trial start. It matches the owner user's USR_XREF.crt_ts, and email sends follow it at fixed offsets.
Acquisition source or channel code (6 levels). This is not a plan reference.
Account geography; references GEO_REF.
Company employee-size band (7 ordinal levels). This is not a geography reference.
User who performed the event.
Event or feature type code (15 types). This is not a geography reference.
Event timestamp.
Event or session duration in milliseconds (100 ms to about 115 s).
Account the email was sent to.
Email template or sequence step (8 steps). Steps 1 and 2 reach all 20000 accounts and later steps reach fewer, which suggests a drip sequence. This is not a geography reference.
Email send time. The examples sit at a fixed time of day offset from account creation (day 1, 2, 4, ...).
Whether the email was opened (about 31%).
Whether a link in the email was clicked (about 9%).
Geography identifier.
Region grouping code (5 regions, e.g. continents). This is not a plan reference.
Time-zone offset from UTC in hours (-9 to +10).
Invoice line identifier.
Subscription being billed.

Line type. Types 1 and 3 each have 25360 rows, equal to the number of distinct bill_ts, so they appear once per billing cycle (e.g. base charge plus tax or discount). Type 2 may be seat add-ons; type 4 is rare (possibly credit or refund). This is not a plan reference.
Line amount, likely in minor currency units (e.g. 7900 = 79.00, matching a list price). Negative values are credits or discounts.
Billing date of the invoice cycle (about every 30 days; the first cycle equals the subscription start).
Plan identifier.
Monthly list price of the plan (15 to 999).
Maximum seats or users allowed on the plan.
Ordinal tier level; two plans share tier 1. This is a ranking attribute, not a self-reference.
Subscription identifier.
Account that holds the paid subscription (unique, so at most one per account).
Plan subscribed to.
Paid subscription start, i.e. the conversion timestamp used to define the outcome label.
Subscription end or cancellation time; null while the subscription is still active.
Subscription status. Code 2 has 729 rows, matching the 729 non-null end_ts, so 2 is likely cancelled; 1 is likely active; 3 may be paused or past due.
Support ticket number.
Account that raised the ticket.
User who raised the ticket; null (about 20%) when not tied to a known user.
Ticket open time.
Ticket severity or priority (4 levels; direction of the scale unknown).
Customer satisfaction rating from 1 to 5; null when not rated (about 40%).
Ticket close time (never null, so all tickets appear closed).
User identifier.
Account the user belongs to.
User role. Code 1 has exactly 20000 rows, one per account, so it is likely owner or admin; 2 and 3 are likely member or viewer.
User who invited this user; null mostly for account creators.
User creation or join time.

outcome_insights.statement: About 21% of accounts (4229 of 20000) have a SUB_HDR row, so the overall paid-conversion rate is roughly one in five. The rate for the defined label (conversion in days 5 to 21 among accounts not yet converted) will differ and must be computed from SUB_HDR.st_ts relative to ACCT_MSTR.crt_ts.

Email sequence volume falls after the first two templates (20000, 20000, then 19588, 19098, ...). This suggests sends may be suppressed once an account converts or churns from the trial. Later-template counts are therefore probably entangled with the outcome and should only be used if they were sent before the day-5 cutoff.

Early-trial engagement signals are plausible candidate predictors of conversion, but no predictive evidence was supplied, so any association is untested. Candidates include usage event counts and durations by evt_cd, the number of invited users (inv_by), email opens and clicks, and support tickets with their CSAT.
INV_LN, SUB_HDR.pln_id, stat_cd and end_ts exist only for converted accounts and describe events after conversion. They would leak the label and must be excluded from features.
Firmographic attributes (seg_cd, emp_band, src_cd, geo_ref) are available at signup and may be associated with conversion. The meaning of each code is unconfirmed.

ambiguities.description: Meanings of the coded columns seg_cd, src_cd, emp_band, evt_cd, tmpl_cd, ln_typ, stat_cd, role_cd and sev are unknown. Their value overlaps with PLN_REF and GEO_REF keys are almost certainly coincidental.
The ACCT_MSTR.geo_ref to GEO_REF link rests on name and range match only (small integer range, range_density 1.0).

It is unclear whether SUB_HDR.st_ts is the true conversion moment or the first billing date after a grace period, and whether accounts can have multiple or renewed subscriptions that are not captured (acct_key is unique in SUB_HDR).
Currency and scale of INV_LN.amt (cents vs units) are unclear, as is the meaning of negative amounts.
The trial length is not stated. It is unknown whether conversions can happen after day 21, and whether stat_cd=3 means paused, past-due or something else.
About 1% of USR_XREF users have no events, and 19.8% of tickets have no user. It is unclear whether these represent inactive users or missing data.

next_investigations: Build the label: for each account compute days from ACCT_MSTR.crt_ts to SUB_HDR.st_ts; exclude accounts converted before day 5; flag conversions in days 5 to 21. Check the base rate and the distribution of conversion day.

Construct features strictly from data before the cutoff (crt_ts + 5 days): event counts, distinct evt_cd, dur_ms and active days per account via USR_XREF; invited users and role mix; email opens and clicks for sends before the cutoff; tickets opened before the cutoff. Then measure univariate associations with the label.
Verify whether email template sends stop after conversion (compare snd_ts with SUB_HDR.st_ts) to quantify leakage risk.
Profile conversion rate by seg_cd, emp_band, src_cd and GEO_REF.rgn_cd, and ask business owners for the code dictionaries.
Check the INV_LN structure per billing cycle (ln_typ 1/3 pairing, amounts vs PLN_REF.list_px * 100) to confirm the amount scale and line types.
Confirm with the business whether role_cd=1 is the account owner and whether USR_XREF.crt_ts for that user equals ACCT_MSTR.crt_ts for every account.
